title: Leaked: How Silicon Valley Elites Bankrolled an Anti-Migrant, Pro-Israel Propaganda Machine
gist: A WIRED investigation, based on leaked V24 financial records, internal chats and donor correspondence, reports that Warsaw-based right-wing X account Visegrad24 (founder Stefan Tompson) chose a pro-Israel editorial line after October 7 explicitly to fundraise, then raised over $1 million via a Delaware 501(c)(3) (Intermarium Foundation), with donations linked to Silicon Valley and Wall Street figures and dark-money vehicles such as DonorsTrust. It shows how virality on Elon Musk's X can be monetized through elite pro-Israel group chats, while V24's off-X ventures largely flopped and its niche grows more contested. Tompson issued a blanket denial via a lawyer.

insights.claim: Visegrad24's ~400 posts in the first three days of the Gaza war racked up 370 million views, per a University of Washington analysis, letting a 641,000-follower Polish account briefly out-reach CNN, The New York Times and the BBC on X.
insights.speaker: James Jackson
insights.so_what: Shows how small, high-volume accounts can capture breaking-news attention on X during conflicts, eclipsing legacy media reach.
insights.quote: those 400 posts racked up an astonishing 370 million views
insights.locator: In the conflict’s first three days

insights.claim: According to texts reviewed by WIRED, Visegrad24 founder Stefan Tompson weighed four editorial options on the Israel–Hamas war and framed the pro-Israel choice around fundraising, writing that his goal was to fundraise off the war.
insights.speaker: James Jackson
insights.so_what: Evidence that partisan war coverage on social platforms can be driven by monetization calculus rather than conviction.
insights.quote: My goal is to fundraise off of this
insights.locator: Ultimately, the founder reasoned a way through

insights.claim: Per messages reviewed by WIRED, Tompson privately expressed qualms about Israel's conduct in the war in October 2023 even while steering V24 toward a pro-Israel line.
insights.speaker: James Jackson
insights.so_what: Highlights the gap between private views and public editorial lines at influential partisan media accounts.
insights.quote: And the Israelis do seem to be doing some vicious things.
insights.locator: With the Israel situation

insights.claim: Tompson concluded that V24 had failed to monetize its Ukraine-war traffic surge in 2022 and resolved not to repeat that mistake when it used the same flood-the-zone strategy after October 7.
insights.speaker: James Jackson
insights.so_what: Conflict-driven virality is a repeatable playbook; the monetization step is what changed after 2022.
insights.quote: we missed the boat with Ukraine
insights.locator: By that fall, Tompson seems to have realized

insights.claim: Per WIRED's documents, when a colleague asked about taking Saudi and UAE money, Tompson replied to play both sides, with himself handling the Jewish side and the colleague the Arabs.
insights.speaker: James Jackson
insights.so_what: Suggests V24's funding approach was opportunistic across geopolitical camps.
insights.locator: While Tompson was fundraising away

themes.theme: Silicon Valley and Wall Street donors

insights.claim: Tompson told a confidant he had joined pro-Israel VC group chats including Jewish Alliances, and claimed membership in Builders for Israel, a WhatsApp thread reported by Puck to include Sheryl Sandberg, Bill Ackman and David Marcus.
insights.speaker: James Jackson
insights.so_what: Elite tech/finance group chats functioned as an informal funding and amplification network for pro-Israel online media after October 7.
insights.quote: V24 is such a big part of the Israeli PR they all know what it is now.
insights.locator: In late November 2023

insights.claim: Sequoia Capital general partner Shaun Maguire recommended Visegrad24 in the Jewish Alliances chat and privately offered Tompson $25,000, but told WIRED he ultimately did not donate for compliance reasons.
insights.speaker: James Jackson
insights.so_what: Reputational and compliance risk for VC firms whose partners engage in political 'information warfare' funding.
insights.quote: I wasn't able to for compliance reasons
insights.locator: On Jewish Alliances, Tompson came personally recommended

insights.claim: WIRED reports Maguire had made introductions that eventually helped connect the Israel Defense Forces with Starlink in the earliest days of the Gaza war, and later said October 7 galvanized him toward 'information warfare' for Israel.
insights.speaker: James Jackson
insights.so_what: Ties between Musk-affiliated companies' investors and wartime information operations are a governance and geopolitical exposure point.
insights.locator: On Jewish Alliances, Tompson came personally recommended

insights.claim: Financial records reviewed by WIRED show donations of $50,000 and $200,000 roughly lining up with Tompson's messages about money from Ribbit Capital founder Micky Malka, who did not respond to requests for comment.
insights.speaker: James Jackson
insights.so_what: Fintech/crypto investor capital flowing into political media is a reputational watch-point for the firms involved.
insights.locator: As a platform for fundraising

insights.claim: Records indicate V24 secured a $20,000 donation from Hindenberg Research plus $15,000 linked to an email associated with founder Nathan Anderson, who did not respond to requests for comment.
insights.speaker: James Jackson
insights.so_what: A prominent short seller's links to a far-right-adjacent media outlet is a reputational data point.
insights.locator: As a platform for fundraising

insights.claim: GiveButter notifications showed donations to V24 linked to emails associated with Michael Sinensky, Neil Blumenthal, Nir Zohar, Josh Wolfe and Matt Ocko; Sinensky and Blumenthal declined comment, Zohar's reps said they had no record of donating, and Wolfe and Ocko neither confirmed nor denied while disputing the 'far right' label.
insights.speaker: James Jackson
insights.so_what: Named tech executives and VCs face potential reputational exposure from leaked donor data.
insights.quote: I don't fund or support ‘far right’ groups
insights.locator: Notifications from GiveButter

insights.claim: Tompson claimed a 'soft commitment' from investor Daniel Gross, but Gross's representatives told WIRED they have no record of a donation.
insights.speaker: James Jackson
insights.so_what: Claimed backers versus confirmed donors should be distinguished; not all names are verified contributors.
insights.locator: Tompson also claimed he had a “soft commitment”

insights.claim: V24 received donations through a 501(c)(3) called the Intermarium Foundation (Pennsylvania-headquartered, Delaware-domiciled), which took in over a million dollars, much of it via anonymous donor-advised funds.
insights.speaker: James Jackson
insights.so_what: Donor-advised funds let political media raise large sums without donor disclosure, obscuring influence funding.
insights.locator: To receive its donations

insights.claim: Foundation documents show the Intermarium Foundation received $175,000 from DonorsTrust in November 2024, and documents suggest $172,000 came from the Giving Back Fund.
insights.speaker: James Jackson
insights.so_what: DonorsTrust's role as 'dark money ATM' of the American right links US conservative philanthropy to European far-right online media.
insights.locator: Foundation documents show that in November 2024

insights.claim: Polish outlets reported that Prime Minister Mateusz Morawiecki's office tried to route about $300,000 in 2022 and just under $600,000 in 2023 to V24-affiliated projects via the Action-Life Foundation, with the 2023 grant recalled after outcry; Tompson has said he never got a penny from the Polish state.
insights.speaker: James Jackson
insights.so_what: State patronage of nominally independent online media is a risk that shifts with elections, as the Law and Justice Party's 2023 loss showed.
insights.locator: V24’s boosted reach didn’t bring an end

insights.claim: A WIRED–Bright Data analysis found Elon Musk engaged with Visegrad24 at least three times more than any of ~30 prominent European far-right accounts over a 45-day window ending January 2025.
insights.speaker: James Jackson
insights.so_what: Owner engagement on X can massively amplify niche political accounts, a platform-governance risk for advertisers.
insights.locator: From its headquarters in Warsaw

insights.claim: Visegrad24 ranks 32nd among all X accounts in the number of community notes attached to its posts, and spread debunked claims during the Ukraine war, such as a false Leonardo DiCaprio $10 million donation.
insights.speaker: James Jackson
insights.so_what: Misinformation-heavy accounts thriving on X sustain brand-safety concerns for the platform.
insights.locator: Another dubious mark of distinction

insights.claim: Visegrad24's follower count tripled from 80,000 to 250,000 within weeks of Russia's 2022 invasion of Ukraine and has since grown to 2.1 million on X.
insights.speaker: James Jackson
insights.so_what: Conflict events are the key growth catalysts for breaking-news accounts on X.
insights.locator: In the three years since October 7

insights.claim: During the June 2025 Israel–Iran war, V24 heavily promoted exiled Crown Prince Reza Pahlavi, including a post about defecting Iranian officers that drew over a million views, while Citizen Lab and Haaretz reported Israel was likely behind a pro-Pahlavi influence operation; Tompson denied foreign-state funding with a sarcastic reply.
insights.speaker: James Jackson
insights.so_what: Online regime-change narratives around Iran overlapped with reported state influence operations, a geopolitical information-war signal.
insights.locator: On June 13, 2025, Israel leaped into the wider conflict

insights.claim: Outside X, V24's ventures largely struggled: its YouTube channel has about 180,000 subscribers with most videos under 10,000 views, V24 Investigations is dormant, and spinoffs like Middle East 24 often fail to top 10 likes.
insights.speaker: James Jackson
insights.so_what: Platform-dependent media brands rarely transfer reach across platforms; V24's value is concentrated on X.
insights.locator: In reality, many of Visegrad’s new ventures

insights.claim: Garbage Day founder Ryan Broderick says real-time crisis coverage on X has become a crowded market due to OSINT 'monitoring the situation' accounts, so an October 7–style V24 blitz would now struggle to break through.
insights.speaker: James Jackson
insights.so_what: Breaking-news attention on X is commoditizing, eroding first-mover advantages of accounts like V24.
insights.quote: They’re operating in an extremely competitive space
insights.locator: In the three years since October 7

insights.claim: WIRED argues that support for Israel has become an increasingly isolating position on the global far right, which has leaned further into antisemitism, illustrated by creator Lord Miles walking away from a collaboration with Tompson over pro-Israel fundraising.
insights.speaker: James Jackson
insights.so_what: Fracturing within the far-right mediasphere over Israel may constrain pro-Israel right-wing outlets' audience growth.
